newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa-UAP no plans to sell DLJ.
newsitem.headline: Axa-UAP no plans to sell DLJ.

text.p: French insurer Axa-UAP said on Wednesday it did not plan to sell Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette (DLJ), the investment bank of its U.S. unit The Equitable, unless it got an "irresistible" offer.
"DLJ is not part of our core business. But it's doing remarkably well. We don't have any intention today of selling it unless we get an irresistible offer," AXA-UAP chairman Claude Bebear said.
He was speaking at a news conference at which the group unveiled its 1996 results.
He said Axa-UAP intended to focus on its core insurance businesses but was making "a small judicious exception" in the case of DLJ which is strongly profitable.
DLJ's after tax operating earnings for 1996 rose to a record $291.3 million for 1996, 58 percent above the $183.8 million it posted the previous year.
